parameters.description: An AcPrintRange constant that specifies the range to print. The default value is acPrintAll.

parameters.name: PageFrom
parameters.description: The first page to print. A numeric expression that's a valid page number in the active form or datasheet. This argument is required if you specify acPages for the _PrintRange_ argument.

parameters.name: PageTo
parameters.description: The last page to print. A numeric expression that's a valid page number in the active form or datasheet. This argument is required if you specify acPages for the _PrintRange_ argument.

parameters.name: PrintQuality
parameters.description: An AcPrintQuality constant that specifies the print quality. The default value is acHigh.

parameters.name: Copies
parameters.description: The number of copies to print. If you leave this argument blank, the default (1) is assumed.

parameters.name: CollateCopies
parameters.description: Use True (1) to collate copies and False (0) to print without collating. If you leave this argument blank, the default (True) is assumed.

methods.name: Quit
methods.description: The Quit method quits Microsoft Access. You can select one of several options for saving a database object before quitting.

parameters.name: Options
parameters.description: An AcQuitOption constant that indicates the action to take when quitting Access. The default value is acQuitSaveAll.

methods.name: Requery
methods.description: Carries out the Requery action in Visual Basic.

parameters.name: ControlName
parameters.description: A string expression that's the name of a control on the active object.

methods.name: RepaintObject
methods.description: The RepaintObject method carries out the RepaintObject action in Visual Basic.

parameters.name: ObjectType
parameters.description: An AcObjectType constant that specifies the type of object to repaint.

parameters.name: ObjectName
parameters.description: A string expression that's the valid name of an object of the type selected by the _ObjectType_ argument.

methods.name: Rename
methods.signature: Rename(NewName As Variant, [ObjectType As AcObjectType], [OldName As Variant])
methods.description: The Rename method carries out the Rename action in Visual Basic.

parameters.name: NewName
parameters.description: A string expression that's the new name for the object that you want to rename. The name must follow the object-naming rules for Microsoft Access objects.

parameters.name: ObjectType
parameters.description: An AcObjectType constant that specifies the type of object to rename. The default value is acDefault.

parameters.name: OldName
parameters.description: A string expression that's the valid name of an object of the type specified by the _ObjectType_ argument. If you execute Visual Basic code containing the Rename method in a library database, Access looks for the object with this name first in the library database, and then in the current database.

methods.name: Restore
methods.description: The Restore method carries out the Restore action in Visual Basic.

methods.name: RunMacro
methods.signature: RunMacro(MacroName As Variant, [RepeatCount As Variant], [RepeatExpression As Variant])
methods.description: The RunMacro method carries out the RunMacro action in Visual Basic.

parameters.name: MacroName
parameters.description: A string expression that's the valid name of a macro in the current database. If you run Visual Basic code containing the RunMacro method in a library database, Microsoft Access looks for the macro with this name in the library database and doesn't look for it in the current database.

parameters.name: RepeatCount
parameters.description: A numeric expression that evaluates to an integer, which is the number of times the macro will run.

parameters.name: RepeatExpression
parameters.description: A numeric expression that's evaluated each time the macro runs. When it evaluates to False (0), the macro stops running.

methods.name: RunSQL
methods.description: The RunSQL method carries out the RunSQL action in Visual Basic.

parameters.name: SQLStatement
parameters.description: A string expression that's a valid SQL statement for an action query or a data-definition query. It uses an INSERT INTO, DELETE, SELECT...INTO, UPDATE, CREATE TABLE, ALTER TABLE, DROP TABLE, CREATE INDEX, or DROP INDEX statement. Include an IN clause if you want to access another database.

parameters.name: UseTransaction
parameters.description: Use True (1) to include this query in a transaction. Use False (0) if you don't want to use a transaction. If you leave this argument blank, the default (True) is assumed.

methods.name: SelectObject
methods.signature: SelectObject(ObjectType As AcObjectType, [ObjectName As Variant], [InDatabaseWindow As Variant])
methods.description: The SelectObject method carries out the SelectObject action in Visual Basic.

parameters.name: ObjectType
parameters.description: An AcObjectType constant that specifies the type of object that you want to select.

parameters.name: ObjectName
parameters.description: A string expression that's the valid name of an object of the type selected by the _ObjectType_ argument. This is a required argument, unless you specify True (1) for the _InNavigationPane_ argument.

methods.name: SetWarnings
methods.description: The SetWarnings method carries out the SetWarnings action in Visual Basic.

parameters.name: WarningsOn
parameters.description: Use True (1) to turn on the display of system messages and False (0) to turn it off.

methods.name: ShowAllRecords
methods.description: The ShowAllRecords method carries out the ShowAllRecords action in Visual Basic.

methods.name: TransferDatabase
methods.signature: TransferDatabase([TransferType As AcDataTransferType], [DatabaseType As Variant], [DatabaseName As Variant], [ObjectType As AcObjectType], [Source As Variant], [Destination As Variant], [StructureOnly As Variant], [StoreLogin As Variant])
methods.description: The TransferDatabase method carries out the TransferDatabase action in Visual Basic.

parameters.name: TransferType
parameters.description: The type of transfer you want to make.

parameters.name: DatabaseType
parameters.description:
A string expression that's the name of one of the types of databases that you can use to import, export, or link data. The _DatabaseType_ parameter is required for exporting and link data actions but not required for importing actions. The types or databases are:

  • Microsoft Access (default)

  • Jet 2.x

  • Jet 3.x

  • dBase III

  • dBase IV

  • dBase 5.0

  • Paradox 3.x

  • Paradox 4.x

  • Paradox 5.x

  • Paradox 7.x

  • ODBC Database

  • WSS (SharePoint)

parameters.name: DatabaseName
parameters.description: A string expression that's the full name, including the path (for WSS, Windows SharePoint Services, the URL), of the database that you want to use to import, export, or link data.

parameters.name: ObjectType
parameters.description: The type of object to import or export.

parameters.name: Source
parameters.description: A string expression that's the name of the object whose data you want to import, export, or link.

parameters.name: Destination
parameters.description: A string expression that's the name of the imported, exported, or linked object in the destination database.

parameters.name: StructureOnly
parameters.description: Use True (1) to import or export only the structure of a database table. Use False (0) to import or export the structure of the table and its data. If you leave this argument blank, the default (False) is assumed.

parameters.name: StoreLogin
parameters.description: Use True to store the sign-in identification (ID) and password for an ODBC database in the connection string for a linked table from the database. If you do this, you don't have to sign in each time you open the table. Use False if you don't want to store the sign-in ID and password. If you leave this argument blank, the default (False) is assumed. This argument is available only in Visual Basic.

methods.name: TransferSpreadsheet
methods.signature: TransferSpreadsheet([TransferType As AcDataTransferType], [SpreadsheetType As AcSpreadSheetType], [TableName As Variant], [FileName As Variant], [HasFieldNames As Variant], [Range As Variant], [UseOA As Variant])
methods.description: The TransferSpreadsheet method carries out the TransferSpreadsheet action in Visual Basic.

parameters.name: TransferType
parameters.description: The type of transfer that you want to make. The default value is acImport.

parameters.name: SpreadsheetType
parameters.description: The type of spreadsheet to import from, export to, or link to.

parameters.name: TableName
parameters.description: A string expression that is the name of the Office Access table that you want to import spreadsheet data into, export spreadsheet data from, or link spreadsheet data to, or the Access select query whose results you want to export to a spreadsheet.

parameters.name: FileName
parameters.description: A string expression that's the file name and path of the spreadsheet that you want to import from, export to, or link to.

parameters.name: HasFieldNames
parameters.description: Use True (1) to use the first row of the spreadsheet as field names when importing or linking. Use False (0) to treat the first row of the spreadsheet as normal data. If you leave this argument blank, the default (False) is assumed. When you export Access table or select query data to a spreadsheet, the field names are inserted into the first row of the spreadsheet no matter what you enter for this argument.

parameters.name: Range
parameters.description: A string expression that's a valid range of cells or the name of a range in the spreadsheet. This argument applies only to importing. Leave this argument blank to import the entire spreadsheet. When you export to a spreadsheet, you must leave this argument blank. If you enter a range, the export will fail.

parameters.name: UseOA
parameters.description: This argument is not supported.

methods.name: TransferText
methods.signature: TransferText([TransferType As AcTextTransferType], [SpecificationName As Variant], [TableName As Variant], [FileName As Variant], [HasFieldNames As Variant], [HTMLTableName As Variant], [CodePage As Variant])
methods.description: The TransferText method carries out the TransferText action in Visual Basic.

parameters.name: TransferType
parameters.description: The type of transfer you want to make. You can import data from, export data to, or link to data in delimited or fixed-width text files or HTML files. The default value is acImportDelim. Only acImportDelim, acImportFixed, acExportDelim, acExportFixed, or acExportMerge transfer types are supported in a Microsoft Access project (.adp).

parameters.name: SpecificationName
parameters.description: A string expression that's the name of an import or export specification you've created and saved in the current database. For a fixed-width text file, you must either specify an argument or use a schema.ini file, which must be stored in the same folder as the imported, linked, or exported text file. To create a schema file, you can use the text import/export wizard to create the file. For delimited text files and Microsoft Word mail merge data files, you can leave this argument blank to select the default import/export specifications.

parameters.name: TableName
parameters.description: A string expression that's the name of the Access table you want to import text data to, export text data from, or link text data to, or the Access query whose results you want to export to a text file.

parameters.name: FileName
parameters.description: A string expression that's the full name, including the path, of the text file you want to import from, export to, or link to.

parameters.name: HasFieldNames
parameters.description: Use True (1) to use the first row of the text file as field names when importing, exporting, or linking. Use False (0) to treat the first row of the text file as normal data. If you leave this argument blank, the default (False) is assumed. This argument is ignored for Microsoft Word mail merge data files, which must always contain the field names in the first row.

parameters.name: HTMLTableName
parameters.description: A string expression that's the name of the table or list in the HTML file that you want to import or link. This argument is ignored unless the _TransferType_ argument is set to acImportHTML or acLinkHTML. If you leave this argument blank, the first table or list in the HTML file is imported or linked. The name of the table or list in the HTML file is determined by the text specified by the CAPTION tag, if there's a CAPTION tag. If there's no CAPTION tag, the name is determined by the text specified by the TITLE tag. If more than one table or list has the same name, Access distinguishes them by adding a number to the end of each table or list name; for example, Employees1 and Employees2.

methods.name: DeleteObject
methods.description: The DeleteObject method carries out the DeleteObject action in Visual Basic.

parameters.name: ObjectType
parameters.description: An AcObjectType constant that represents the type of object to delete.

parameters.name: ObjectName
parameters.description: A string expression that's the valid name of an object of the type selected by the _ObjectType_ argument. If you run Visual Basic code containing the DeleteObject method in a library database, Microsoft Access looks for the object with this name first in the library database, and then in the current database.

methods.name: OpenModule
methods.description: The OpenModule method carries out the OpenModule action in Visual Basic.

parameters.name: ModuleName
parameters.description: A string expression that's the valid name of the Visual Basic module that you want to open. If you leave this argument blank, Microsoft Access searches all the standard modules in the database for the procedure that you selected with the _ProcedureName_ argument and opens the module containing the procedure to that procedure. If you execute Visual Basic code containing the OpenModule method in a library database, Access looks for the module with this name first in the library database, and then in the current database.

parameters.name: ProcedureName
parameters.description: A string expression that's the valid name for the procedure that you want to open the module to. If you leave this argument blank, the module opens to the Declarations section.

methods.name: SendObject
methods.signature: SendObject([ObjectType As AcSendObjectType], [ObjectName As Variant], [OutputFormat As Variant], [To As Variant], [Cc As Variant], [Bcc As Variant], [Subject As Variant], [MessageText As Variant], [EditMessage As Variant], [TemplateFile As Variant])
methods.description: The SendObject method carries out the SendObject action in Visual Basic.

parameters.name: ObjectType
parameters.description: An AcSendObjectType constant that specifies the type of object to send.

parameters.name: ObjectName
parameters.description: A string expression that's the valid name of an object of the type selected by the _ObjectType_ argument. If you want to include the active object in the mail message, specify the object's type with the _ObjectType_ argument and leave this argument blank. If you leave both the _ObjectType_ and _ObjectName_ arguments blank (the default constant, acSendNoObject, is assumed for the _ObjectType_ argument), Microsoft Access sends a message to the electronic mail application without an included database object. If you run Visual Basic code containing the SendObject method in a library database, Access looks for the object with this name first in the library database, and then in the current database.

parameters.name: OutputFormat
parameters.description: A constant that specifies the format in which to send the object. Possible values include acFormatHTML, acFormatRTF, acFormatSNP, acFormatTXT, acFormatXLS, acFormatXLSB, acFormatXLSX, acFormatXPS, and acFormatPDF.

parameters.name: To
parameters.description: A string expression that lists the recipients whose names you want to put on the To line in the mail message. Separate the recipient names that you specify in this argument and in the _Cc_ and _Bcc_ arguments with a semicolon (;), or with the list separator set on the Number tab of the Regional Settings Properties dialog box in the Windows Control Panel. If the recipient names aren't recognized by the mail application, the message isn't sent and an error occurs. If you leave this argument blank, Microsoft Access prompts you for the recipients.

parameters.name: Cc
parameters.description: A string expression that lists the recipients whose names you want to put on the Cc line in the mail message. If you leave this argument blank, the Cc line in the mail message is blank.

parameters.name: Bcc
parameters.description: A string expression that lists the recipients whose names you want to put on the Bcc line in the mail message. If you leave this argument blank, the Bcc line in the mail message is blank.

parameters.name: Subject
parameters.description: A string expression containing the text that you want to put on the Subject line in the mail message. If you leave this argument blank, the Subject line in the mail message is blank.

parameters.name: MessageText
parameters.description: A string expression containing the text that you want to include in the body of the mail message, after the object. If you leave this argument blank, the object is all that's included in the body of the mail message.

parameters.name: EditMessage
parameters.description: Use True (1) to open the electronic mail application immediately with the message loaded, so the message can be edited. Use False (0) to send the message without editing it. If you leave this argument blank, the default (True) is assumed.

parameters.name: TemplateFile
parameters.description: A string expression that's the full name, including the path, of the file that you want to use as a template for an HTML file.

methods.name: ShowToolbar
methods.description: The ShowToolbar method carries out the ShowToolbar action in Visual Basic.

parameters.name: ToolbarName
parameters.description: A string expression that's the valid name of a custom toolbar you've created. If you run Visual Basic code containing the ShowToolbar method in a library database, Microsoft Access looks for the toolbar with this name first in the library database, and then in the current database.

parameters.name: Show
parameters.description: An AcShowToolbar constant that specifies whether to display or hide the toolbar and in which views to display or hide it. The default value is acToolbarYes.

methods.name: Save
methods.description: The Save method carries out the Save action in Visual Basic.

parameters.name: ObjectType
parameters.description: An AcObjectType constant that specifies the type of object that you want to save.

parameters.name: ObjectName
parameters.description: A string expression that's the valid name of an object of the type selected by the _ObjectType_ argument.

methods.name: SetMenuItem
methods.signature: SetMenuItem(MenuIndex As Variant, [CommandIndex As Variant], [SubcommandIndex As Variant], [Flag As Variant])
methods.description: The SetMenuItem method carries out the SetMenuItem action in Visual Basic.

parameters.name: MenuIndex
parameters.description: An integer, counting from 0, that is the valid index of a menu on the custom menu bar or global menu bar for the active window, as defined in the menu bar macro for the custom menu bar or global menu bar. If you select a menu with this argument and leave the _CommandIndex_ and _SubcommandIndex_ arguments blank (or set them to 1), you can enable or disable the menu name itself. You can't, however, check or uncheck a menu name (Microsoft Access ignores the acMenuCheck and acMenuUncheck settings for the _Flag_ argument for menu names).

parameters.name: CommandIndex
parameters.description: An integer, counting from 0, that's the valid index of a command on the menu selected by the _MenuIndex_ argument, as defined in the macro group that defines the selected menu for the custom menu bar or global menu bar for the active window.

parameters.name: SubcommandIndex
parameters.description: An integer, counting from 0, that's the valid index of a subcommand in the submenu selected by the _CommandIndex_ argument, as defined in the macro group that defines the selected submenu for the custom menu bar or global menu bar for the active window.

parameters.name: Flag
parameters.description:
The state you want to set the command or subcommand to. Can be one of the following constants:
  • acMenuCheck
  • acMenuGray
  • acMenuUncheck
  • acMenuUngray (default)

methods.name: RunCommand
methods.description: The RunCommand method runs a built-in command.

parameters.name: Command
parameters.description: An AcCommand constant that specifies the command to run.

methods.name: OpenDataAccessPage
methods.description: The OpenDataAccessPage method carries out the OpenDataAccessPage action in Visual Basic.

parameters.name: DataAccessPageName
parameters.description: A string expression that's the valid name of a data access page in the current database. If you execute Visual Basic code containing the OpenDataAccessPage method in a library database, Microsoft Access looks for the form with this name, first in the library database, and then in the current database.

parameters.name: View
parameters.description: The view in which to open the data access page. In Access, this must be set to acDataAccessPageBrowse.

methods.name: OpenView
methods.signature: OpenView(ViewName As Variant, [View As AcView], [DataMode As AcOpenDataMode])
methods.description: The OpenView method carries out the OpenView action in Visual Basic.

parameters.name: ViewName
parameters.description: A string expression that's the valid name of a view in the current database. If you execute Visual Basic code containing the OpenView method in a library database, Microsoft Access looks for the view with this name first in the library database, and then in the current database.

parameters.name: View
parameters.description: An AcView constant that specifies the view in which the view will open. The default value is acViewNormal.

parameters.name: DataMode
parameters.description: An AcOpenDataMode constant that specifies the data entry mode for the view. The default value is acEdit.

methods.name: OpenDiagram
methods.description: The OpenDiagram method carries out the OpenDiagram action in Visual Basic.

parameters.name: DiagramName
parameters.description: A string expression that's the valid name of a database diagram in the current database. If you execute Visual Basic code containing the OpenDiagram method in a library database, Microsoft Access looks for the database diagram with this name first in the library database, and then in the current database.

methods.name: OpenStoredProcedure
methods.signature: OpenStoredProcedure(ProcedureName As Variant, [View As AcView], [DataMode As AcOpenDataMode])
methods.description: The OpenStoredProcedure method carries out the OpenStoredProcedure action in Visual Basic.

parameters.name: ProcedureName
parameters.description: A string expression that's the valid name of a stored procedure in the current database. If you execute Visual Basic code containing the OpenStoredProcedure method in a library database, Microsoft Access looks for the stored procedure with this name first in the library database, and then in the current database.

parameters.name: View
parameters.description: An AcView constant that specifies the view in which the stored procedure will open. The default value is acViewNormal.

parameters.name: DataMode
parameters.description: An AcOpenDataMode constant that specifies the data entry mode for the stored procedure. The default value is acEdit.

methods.name: OpenReport
methods.signature: OpenReport(ReportName As Variant, [View As AcView], [FilterName As Variant], [WhereCondition As Variant], [WindowMode As AcWindowMode], [OpenArgs As Variant])
methods.description: The OpenReport method carries out the OpenReport action in Visual Basic.

parameters.name: ReportName
parameters.description: A string expression that's the valid name of a report in the current database. If you execute Visual Basic code containing the OpenReport method in a library database, Microsoft Access looks for the report with this name first in the library database, and then in the current database.

parameters.name: View
parameters.description: An AcView constant that specifies the view in which the report will open. The default value is acViewNormal.

parameters.name: FilterName
parameters.description: A string expression that's the valid name of a query in the current database.

parameters.name: WhereCondition
parameters.description: A string expression that's a valid SQL WHERE clause without the word WHERE.

parameters.name: WindowMode
parameters.description: An AcWindowMode constant that specifies the mode in which the form opens. The default value is acWindowNormal.

parameters.name: OpenArgs
parameters.description: Sets the OpenArgs property.

methods.name: TransferSQLDatabase
methods.signature: TransferSQLDatabase(Server As Variant, Database As Variant, [UseTrustedConnection As Variant], [Login As Variant], [Password As Variant], [TransferCopyData As Variant])
methods.description: Transfers the entire specified Microsoft SQL Server database to another SQL Server database.

parameters.name: Server
parameters.description: The name of the SQL Server to which the database will be transferred.

parameters.name: Database
parameters.description: The name of the new database on the specified server.

parameters.name: UseTrustedConnection
parameters.description: True if the current connection is using a login with system administrator privileges. If this argument is not True, you must specify a login and password in the _Login_ and _Password_ arguments.

parameters.name: Login
parameters.description: The name of a login on the destination server with system administrator privileges. If _UseTrustedConnection_ is True, this argument is ignored.

parameters.name: Password
parameters.description: The password for the login specified in _Login_. If _UseTrustedConnection_ is True, this argument is ignored.

parameters.name: TransferCopyData
parameters.description: True if all data in the database is transferred to the destination database. If this argument is not True, only the database schema will be transferred.

methods.name: CopyDatabaseFile
methods.signature: CopyDatabaseFile(DatabaseFileName As Variant, [OverwriteExistingFile As Variant], [DisconnectAllUsers As Variant])
methods.description: Copies the database connected to the current project to a Microsoft SQL Server database file for export.

parameters.name: DatabaseFileName
parameters.description: The name of the file (and path) to which the current database is copied. If no path is specified, the current directory is used.

parameters.name: OverwriteExistingFile
parameters.description: Determines whether Microsoft Access overwrites the file specified by _DatabaseFileName_. True to overwrite the existing file. If the file doesn't already exist, this argument is ignored.

parameters.name: DisconnectAllUsers
parameters.description: Determines whether Access disconnects any users connected to the current database to make the copy. True to disconnect other users before copying the database file.

methods.name: OpenFunction
methods.signature: OpenFunction(FunctionName As Variant, [View As AcView], [DataMode As AcOpenDataMode])
methods.description: Opens a user-defined function in a Microsoft SQL Server database for viewing in Microsoft Access.

parameters.name: FunctionName
parameters.description: The name of the function to open.

parameters.name: View
parameters.description: An AcView constant that specifies the view in which to open the function. The default value is acViewNormal.

parameters.name: DataMode
parameters.description: An AcOpenDataMode constant that specifies the mode in which to open the function. The default value is acEdit.

methods.name: ApplyFilter
methods.signature: ApplyFilter([FilterName As Variant], [WhereCondition As Variant], [ControlName As Variant])
methods.description: The ApplyFilter method carries out the ApplyFilter action in Visual Basic.

parameters.name: FilterName
parameters.description: A string expression that is the valid name of a filter or query in the current database. When using this method to apply a server filter, the _FilterName_ argument must be blank.

parameters.name: WhereCondition
parameters.description: A string expression that is a valid SQL WHERE clause without the word WHERE.

methods.name: OutputTo
methods.signature: OutputTo(ObjectType As AcOutputObjectType, [ObjectName As Variant], [OutputFormat As Variant], [OutputFile As Variant], [AutoStart As Variant], [TemplateFile As Variant], [Encoding As Variant], [OutputQuality As AcExportQuality])
methods.description: The OutputTo method carries out the OutputTo action in Visual Basic.

parameters.name: ObjectType
parameters.description: An AcOutputObjectType constant that specifies the type of object to output.

parameters.name: ObjectName
parameters.description: A string expression that's the valid name of an object of the type selected by the _ObjectType_ argument. If you want to output the active object, specify the object's type for the _ObjectType_ argument and leave this argument blank. If you run Visual Basic code containing the OutputTo method in a library database, Microsoft Office Access searches for the object with this name first in the library database, and then in the current database.

parameters.name: OutputFormat
parameters.description: An AcFormat constant that specifies the output format. If you omit this argument, Access prompts you for the output format.

parameters.name: OutputFile
parameters.description: A string expression that's the full name, including the path, of the file that you want to output the object to. If you leave this argument blank, Access prompts you for an output file name.

parameters.name: AutoStart
parameters.description: Use True (1) to start the appropriate Microsoft Windows-based application immediately, with the file specified by the _OutputFile_ argument loaded. Use False (0) if you don't want to start the application. This argument is ignored for Microsoft Internet Information Server (.htx, .idc) files and Microsoft ActiveX Server (.asp) files. If you leave this argument blank, the default (False**) is assumed.

parameters.name: TemplateFile
parameters.description: A string expression that's the full name, including the path, of the file that you want to use as a template for an HTML, HTX, or ASP file.

parameters.name: Encoding
parameters.description: The type of character encoding format that you want used to output the text or HTML data. You can select MS-DOS, Unicode, or Unicode (UTF-8). The MS-DOS argument setting is available only for text files. If you leave this argument blank, Access outputs the data by using the Windows default encoding for text files and the default system encoding for HTML files.

parameters.name: OutputQuality
parameters.description: An AcExportQuality constant that specifies the type of output device to optimize for. The default value is acExportQualityPrint.

methods.name: TransferSharePointList
methods.signature: TransferSharePointList(TransferType As AcSharePointListTransferType, SiteAddress As Variant, ListID As Variant, [ViewID As Variant], [TableName As Variant], [GetLookupDisplayValues As Variant])
methods.description: Use the TransferSharePointList method to import or link data from a SharePoint Foundation site.

parameters.name: TransferType
parameters.description: An AcSharePointListTransferType constant that specifies the type of transfer to make.

parameters.name: SiteAddress
parameters.description: The full path of the SharePoint site.

parameters.name: ListID
parameters.description: The name or GUID of the list to be transferred.

parameters.name: ViewID
parameters.description: The GUID of the view for the list that you want to use. Leave this argument blank to transfer all rows and columns in the list.

parameters.name: TableName
parameters.description: The name you want displayed for the table or linked table in Access.

parameters.name: GetLookupDisplayValues
parameters.description: Specifies whether to transfer display values for Lookup fields instead of the ID used to perform the lookup.

methods.name: CloseDatabase
methods.description: Closes the current database.

methods.name: NavigateTo
methods.description: Use the NavigateTo method to control the display of database objects in the navigation pane.

parameters.name: Category
parameters.description: The category by which you want the navigation pane to display objects.

parameters.name: Group
parameters.description: Determines which objects in the category appear in the navigation pane. If you leave this argument blank, the navigation pane will display all database objects grouped by the criteria that you specify in the _Category_ argument. Examples of valid _Group_ arguments for the various _Category_ arguments are shown in the table under Remarks.

methods.name: SearchForRecord
methods.signature: SearchForRecord([ObjectType As AcDataObjectType], [ObjectName As Variant], [Record As AcRecord], [WhereCondition As Variant])
methods.description: Use the SearchForRecord method to search for a specific record in a table, query, form, or report.

parameters.name: ObjectType
parameters.description: An AcDataObjectType constant that specifies the type of database object in which you are searching. The default value is acActiveDataObject.

parameters.name: ObjectName
parameters.description: The name of the database object that contains the record to search for.

parameters.name: Record
parameters.description: An AcRecord constant that specifies the starting point and direction of the search. The default value is acFirst.

parameters.name: WhereCondition
parameters.description: A string used to locate the record. It's like the WHERE clause in an SQL statement, but without the word WHERE.

methods.name: SetProperty
methods.signature: SetProperty([ControlName As Variant], [Property As AcProperty], [Value As Variant])
methods.description: The SetProperty method carries out the SetProperty action in Visual Basic.

parameters.name: ControlName

types.name: Form
types.description: A Form object refers to a particular Microsoft Access form.
types.remarks: A Form object is a member of the Forms collection, which is a collection of all currently open forms. Within the Forms collection, individual forms are indexed beginning with zero. Refer to an individual Form object in the Forms collection either by referring to the form by name, or by referring to its index within the collection. If you want to refer to a specific form in the Forms collection, it's better to refer to the form by name because a form's collection index may change. If the form name includes a space, the name must be surrounded by brackets ([ ]). Each Form object has a Controls collection, which contains all controls on the form. Refer to a control on a form either by implicitly or explicitly referring to the Controls collection. Your code will be faster if you refer to the Controls collection implicitly. The following examples show two of the ways you might refer to a control named NewData on the form called OrderForm. The next two examples show how you might refer to a control named NewData on a subform ctlSubForm contained in the form called OrderForm.
types.example:
Private Sub cmdSearch_Click()

   Dim db As DAO.Database
   Dim qd As QueryDef
   Dim vWhere As Variant

   Set db = CurrentDb()

   On Error Resume Next
   db.QueryDefs.Delete "Query1"
   On Error GoTo 0

   vWhere = Null

   vWhere = vWhere & " AND [PayeeID]=" + Me.cboPayeeID

   If Nz(Me.txtEndDate, "") <> "" And Nz(Me.txtStartDate, "") <> "" Then
      vWhere = vWhere & " AND [RefundProcessed] Between #" & _
      Me.txtStartDate & "# AND #" & Me.txtEndDate & "#"
   Else
      If Nz(Me.txtEndDate, "") = "" And Nz(Me.txtStartDate, "") <> "" Then
         vWhere = vWhere & " AND [RefundProcessed]>=#" _
                  + Me.txtStartDate & "#"
      Else
         If Nz(Me.txtEndDate, "") <> "" And Nz(Me.txtStartDate, "") = "" Then
            vWhere = vWhere & " AND [RefundProcessed] <=#" _
                     + Me.txtEndDate & "#"
      End If
     End If
   End If

   If Nz(vWhere, "") = "" Then
      MsgBox "There are no search criteria selected." & vbCrLf & vbCrLf & _
             "Search Cancelled.", vbInformation, "Search Canceled."
   Else
      Set qd = db.CreateQueryDef("Query1", "SELECT * FROM tblRefundData? & _
               " WHERE " & Mid(vWhere, 6))
      db.Close
      Set db = Nothing

      DoCmd.OpenQuery "Query1", acViewNormal, acReadOnly
   End If
End Sub

events.name: Load
events.description: Occurs when a form is opened and its records are displayed.

events.name: Current
events.description: Occurs when the focus moves to a record, making it the current record, or when the form is refreshed or requeried.

events.name: BeforeInsert
events.description: The BeforeInsert event occurs when the user types the first character in a new record, but before the record is actually created.

parameters.name: Cancel
parameters.description: The setting determines if the BeforeInsert event occurs. Setting the _Cancel_ argument to True (1) cancels the BeforeInsert event.

events.name: AfterInsert
events.description: The AfterInsert event occurs after a new record is added.

events.name: Delete
events.description: Occurs when the user performs some action, such as pressing the Delete key, to delete a record, but before the record is actually deleted.

parameters.name: Cancel
parameters.description: The setting determines if the Delete event occurs. Setting the _Cancel_ argument to True (1) cancels the Delete event.

events.name: BeforeDelConfirm
events.signature: BeforeDelConfirm(Cancel As Integer, Response As Integer)
events.description: The BeforeDelConfirm event occurs after the user deletes to the buffer one or more records, but before Microsoft Access displays a dialog box asking the user to confirm the deletions.

parameters.name: Cancel
parameters.description: The setting determines if the BeforeDelConfirm event occurs. Setting the _Cancel_ argument to True cancels the BeforeDelConfirm event and prevents the Delete Confirm dialog box from being displayed. If the event is canceled, the original records are restored, but the AfterDelConfirm event still occurs. If _Cancel_ is set to True, the _Response_ argument is ignored. If _Cancel_ is set to False (0), which it is by default, the value in the _Response_ argument is used by Access to determine the type of response to the Delete event.

parameters.name: Response
parameters.description: An intrinsic constant that determines whether Access displays the Delete Confirm dialog box asking if the record should be deleted. acDataErrContinue continues without displaying the Delete Confirm dialog box. Setting the _Cancel_ argument to False and the _Response_ argument to acDataErrContinue enables Microsoft Access to delete records without prompting the user. acDataErrDisplay displays the Delete Confirm dialog box. The default value is acDataErrDisplay.

events.name: AfterDelConfirm
events.description: The AfterDelConfirm event occurs after the user confirms that the deletions and the records are actually deleted or when the deletions are canceled.

parameters.name: Status
parameters.description: An intrinsic constant that indicates whether a record has been deleted. acDeleteOK indicates that the deletion was successful. acDeleteCancel indicates that the deletion was canceled in Visual Basic. acDeleteUserCancel indicates that the deletion was canceled by the user.

events.name: Open
events.description: The Open event occurs when a form is opened, but before the first record is displayed.

parameters.name: Cancel
parameters.description: The setting determines if the opening of the form or report occurs. Setting the _Cancel_ argument to True (1) cancels the opening of the form or report.

events.name: Resize
events.description: The Resize event occurs when a form is opened and whenever the size of a form changes.

events.name: Unload
events.description: The Unload event occurs after a form is closed but before it's removed from the screen. When the form is reloaded, Microsoft Access redisplays the form and reinitializes the contents of all its controls.

parameters.name: Cancel
parameters.description: Set to True to cancel the Unload event.

events.name: Close
events.description: The Close event occurs when a form is closed and removed from the screen.

events.name: Activate
events.description: The Activate event occurs when a form receives the focus and becomes the active window.

events.name: Deactivate
events.description: The Deactivate event occurs when a form loses the focus to a Table, Query, Form, Report, Macro, or Module window, or to the Database window.

events.name: GotFocus
events.description: The GotFocus event occurs when the specified object receives the focus.

events.name: LostFocus
events.description: The LostFocus event occurs when the specified object loses the focus.

events.name: Click
events.description: The Click event occurs when the user presses and then releases a mouse button over an object.

events.name: DblClick
events.description: The DblClick event occurs when the user presses and releases the left mouse button twice over an object within the double-click time limit of the system.

parameters.name: Cancel
parameters.description: The setting determines if the DblClick event occurs. Setting the _Cancel_ argument to True (1) cancels the DblClick event.

events.name: MouseDown
events.signature: MouseDown(Button As Integer, Shift As Integer, X As Single, Y As Single)
events.description: The MouseDown event occurs when the user presses a mouse button.

parameters.name: Button
parameters.description:
The button that was pressed to trigger the event. If you need to test for the _Button_ argument, you can use one of the following intrinsic constants as bit masks:

  • acLeftButton The bit mask for the left mouse button.

  • acRightButton The bit mask for the right mouse button.

  • acMiddleButton The bit mask for the middle mouse button.

parameters.name: Shift
parameters.description:
The state of the Shift, Ctrl, and Alt keys when the button specified by the _Button_ argument was pressed or released. If you need to test for the _Shift_ argument, you can use one of the following intrinsic constants as bit masks:

  • acShiftMask The bit mask for the Shift key.

  • acCtrlMask The bit mask for the Ctrl key.

  • acAltMask The bit mask for the Alt key.

parameters.name: X
parameters.description: The _x_ coordinate for the current location of the mouse pointer, in twips.

parameters.name: Y
parameters.description: The _y_ coordinate for the current location of the mouse pointer, in twips.

parameters.name: Shift
parameters.description:
The state of the Shift, Ctrl, and Alt keys when the button specified by the _Button_ argument was pressed or released. If you need to test for the _Shift_ argument, you can use one of the following intrinsic constants as bit masks:

  • acShiftMask The bit mask for the Shift key.

  • acCtrlMask The bit mask for the Ctrl key.

  • acAltMask The bit mask for the Alt key.

parameters.name: X
parameters.description: The _x_ coordinate for the current location of the mouse pointer, in twips.

parameters.name: Y

events.name: KeyDown
events.signature: KeyDown(KeyCode As Integer, Shift As Integer)
events.description: The KeyDown event occurs when the user presses a key while a form or control has the focus. This event also occurs if you send a keystroke to a form or control by using the SendKeys action in a macro or the SendKeys statement in Visual Basic.

parameters.name: KeyCode
parameters.description: A key code, such as vbKeyF1 (the F1 key) or vbKeyHome (the Home key). To specify key codes, use the intrinsic constants shown in the Object Browser. You can prevent an object from receiving a keystroke by setting _KeyCode_ to 0.

parameters.name: Shift
parameters.description:
The state of the Shift, Ctrl, and Alt keys at the time of the event. If you need to test for the _Shift_ argument, you can use one of the following intrinsic constants as bit masks:

  • acShiftMask The bit mask for the Shift key.

  • acCtrlMask The bit mask for the Ctrl key.

  • acAltMask The bit mask for the Alt key.

events.name: KeyPress
events.description: The KeyPress event occurs when the user presses and releases a key or key combination that corresponds to an ANSI code while a form or control has the focus. This event also occurs if you send an ANSI keystroke to a form or control by using the SendKeys action in a macro or the SendKeys statement in Visual Basic.

parameters.name: KeyAscii
parameters.description: Returns a numeric ANSI key code. The _KeyAscii_ argument is passed by reference; changing it sends a different character to the object. Setting the _KeyAscii_ argument to 0 cancels the keystroke so that the object doesn't recognize that a key was pressed.

events.name: KeyUp
events.signature: KeyUp(KeyCode As Integer, Shift As Integer)
events.description: The KeyUp event occurs when the user releases a key while a form or control has the focus. This event also occurs if you send a keystroke to a form or control by using the SendKeys action in a macro or the SendKeys statement in Visual Basic.

parameters.name: KeyCode
parameters.description: A key code, such as vbKeyF1 (the F1 key) or vbKeyHome (the Home key). To specify key codes, use the intrinsic constants shown in the Object Browser. You can prevent an object from receiving a keystroke by setting _KeyCode_ to 0.

parameters.name: Shift
parameters.description:
The state of the Shift, Ctrl, and Alt keys at the time of the event. If you need to test for the _Shift_ argument, you can use one of the following intrinsic constants as bit masks:

  • acShiftMask The bit mask for the Shift key.

  • acCtrlMask The bit mask for the Ctrl key.

  • acAltMask The bit mask for the Alt key.

events.name: Error
events.signature: Error(DataErr As Integer, Response As Integer)
events.description: The Error event occurs when a run-time error is produced in Microsoft Access when a form has the focus.

parameters.name: DataErr
parameters.description: The error code returned by the Err object when an error occurs. Use the _DataErr_ argument with the Error function to map the number to the corresponding error message.

parameters.name: Response
parameters.description:

types.name: FormatCondition
types.description: The FormatCondition object represents a conditional format of a combo box or text box control and is a member of the FormatConditions collection.
types.remarks: Use the FormatConditions (_index_), where _index_ is the index number of the conditional format, to return a FormatCondition object. Use the Add method to create a new conditional format. Use the Modify method to change one of the formats, or the Delete method to delete a format. properties.name: FontBold
properties.description: Use the FontBold property to specify whether a font appears in a bold style in the following situations:

properties.name: FontItalic

methods.signature: Modify(Type As AcFormatConditionType, [Operator As AcFormatConditionOperator], [Expression1 As Variant], [Expression2 As Variant])

types.name: Forms
types.description: The Forms collection contains all the currently open forms in a Microsoft Access database.
types.remarks: Use the Forms collection in Visual Basic or in an expression to refer to forms that are currently open. For example, you can enumerate the Forms collection to set or return the values of properties of individual forms in the collection. Refer to an individual Form object in the Forms collection either by referring to the form by name, or by referring to its index within the collection. If you want to refer to a specific form in the Forms collection, it's better to refer to the form by name because a form's collection index may change. The Forms collection is indexed beginning with zero. If you refer to a form by its index, the first form opened is Forms(0), the second form opened is Forms(1), and so on. If you opened Form1 and then opened Form2, Form2 would be referenced in the Forms collection by its index as Forms(1). If you then closed Form1, Form2 would be referenced in the Forms collection by its index as Forms(0). You can't add or delete a Form object from the Forms collection.

types.name: GroupLevel
types.description: Use the GroupLevel property in Visual Basic to refer to the group level that you are grouping or sorting on in a report.
types.remarks: The GroupLevel property setting is an array in which each entry identifies a group level. To refer to a group level, use this syntax: GroupLevel (_n_) The number _n_ is the group level, starting with 0. The first field or expression that you group on is group level 0, the second is group level 1, and so on. You can have up to 10 group levels (0 to 9). The following sample settings show how you use the GroupLevel property to refer to a group level. Use this property only by using Visual Basic to set the SortOrder, GroupOn, GroupInterval, KeepTogether, and ControlSource properties. You set these properties in the Open event procedure of a report. In reports, you can group or sort on more than one field or expression. Each field or expression that you group or sort on is a group level. You specify the fields and expressions to sort and group on by using the CreateGroupLevel method. If a group is already defined for a report (the GroupLevel property is set to 0), you can use the ControlSource property to change the group level in the report's Open event procedure.

properties.description: Use the Application property to access the active Microsoft Access Application object and its related properties. Read-only Application object.

properties.name: ControlSource
properties.description: Use the ControlSource property to specify what data appears in a control. You can display and edit data bound to a field in a table, query, or SQL statement. You can also display the result of an expression. Read/write String.

properties.name: SortOrder
properties.description: You use the SortOrder property to specify the sort order for fields and expressions in a report. For example, if you are printing a list of suppliers, you can sort the records alphabetically by company name. Read/write Boolean.

properties.name: GroupHeader
properties.description: Use the GroupHeader property to create a group header for a selected field or expression in a report. Read/write Boolean.

properties.name: GroupFooter
properties.description: Use the GroupFooter property to create a group footer for a selected field or expression in a report. Read/write Boolean.

properties.name: GroupOn
properties.description: Use the GroupOn property in a report to specify how to group data in a field or expression by data type. For example, this property lets you group a Date field by month. Read/write Integer.

properties.name: GroupInterval
properties.description: Use the GroupInterval property with the GroupOn property to specify how records are grouped in a report. Read/write Long.

properties.name: KeepTogether
properties.description: Use the KeepTogether property for a group in a report to keep parts of a group (including the group header, detail section, and group footer) together on the same page. For example, you might want a group header to always be printed on the same page with the first detail section. Read/write Byte.

properties.name: SubAddress
properties.description: Use the SubAddress property to specify or determine a location within the target document specified by the Address property. Read/write String.

properties.name: Address
properties.description: Use the Address property to specify or determine the path to an object, document, webpage, or other destination for a Hyperlink object associated with a command button, image control, or label control. Read/write String.

properties.name: EmailSubject
properties.description: Use the EmailSubject property to specify or return the email subject line of a hyperlink to an object, document, webpage, or other destination for a command button, image control, or label control. Read/write String.

properties.name: ScreenTip
properties.description: Use the ScreenTip property to specify or determine the text that is displayed when you move the cursor over a hyperlink control. Read/write String.

properties.name: TextToDisplay
properties.description: Use the TextToDisplay property to specify or determine the display text for a hyperlink. Read/write String.

methods.name: AddToFavorites
methods.description: The AddToFavorites method adds a hyperlink address to the Favorites folder.

methods.name: Follow
methods.signature: Follow([NewWindow As Boolean], [AddHistory As Boolean], [ExtraInfo As Variant], [Method As MsoExtraInfoMethod], [HeaderInfo As String])
methods.description: The Follow method opens the document or webpage specified by a hyperlink address associated with a control on a form or report.

parameters.name: NewWindow
parameters.description: True (1) opens the document in a new window and False (0) opens the document in the current window. The default is False.

parameters.name: AddHistory
parameters.description: True adds the hyperlink to the History folder and False doesn't add the hyperlink to the History folder. The default is True.

parameters.name: ExtraInfo
parameters.description: A string or an array of Byte data that specifies additional information for navigating to a hyperlink. For example, this argument may be used to specify a search parameter for an .ASP or .IDC file. In your web browser, the _ExtraInfo_ argument may appear after the hyperlink address, separated from the address by a question mark (?). You don't need to include the question mark when you specify the _ExtraInfo_ argument.

parameters.name: Method
parameters.description: An MsoExtraInfoMethod constant that specifies how the _ExtraInfo_ argument is attached. The default is msoMethodGet.

parameters.name: HeaderInfo
parameters.description: Specifies header information. By default, the _HeaderInfo_ argument is a zero-length string (" ").

methods.name: CreateNewDocument
methods.signature: CreateNewDocument(FileName As String, EditNow As Boolean, Overwrite As Boolean)
methods.description: Use the CreateNewDocument method to create a new document associated with a specified hyperlink.

parameters.name: FileName
parameters.description:
The name and path of the document. The type of document format that you want to use can be determined by the extension used with the file name to output the data. You can create the following:
  • HTML (\.htm)
  • Microsoft Active Server Pages (\.asp)
  • Microsoft Excel (\.xls)
  • Microsoft IIS (\.htx, \.idc)
  • MS-DOS Text (\.txt)
  • Rich Text Format (\*.rtf)
Modules can be output only to MS-DOS text format. Microsoft Internet Information Server and Microsoft Active Server formats are available only for tables, queries, and forms.

parameters.name: EditNow
parameters.description: True opens the document in Design view, and False stores the new document in the specified database directory. The default is True.

parameters.name: Overwrite
parameters.description: True overwrites an existing document if the _FileName_ argument identifies an existing document, and False requires that the _FileName_ argument specify a new file name. The default is False.

types.name: Image
types.description: This object corresponds to an image control. The image control can add a picture to a form or report. For example, you could include an image control for a logo on an Invoice report.
types.remarks: Use the image control or an Unbound object frame for unbound pictures. The advantage of using the image control is that it's faster to display. The advantage of using the unbound object frame is that you can edit the object directly from the form or report.

types.name: ImportExportSpecification
types.description: Represents a saved import or export operation.
types.remarks: An ImportExportSpecification object contains all the information that Microsoft Access needs to repeat an import or export operation without your having to provide any input. For example, an import specification that imports data from a Microsoft Office Excel 2007 workbook stores the name of the source Excel file, the name of the destination database, and other details, such as whether you appended to or created a new table, primary key information, field names, and so on. Use the Add method of the ImportExportSpecifications collection to create a new ImportExportSpecification object. Use the Execute method to run a saved import or export operation.

types.name: Label
types.description: This object corresponds to a label control. Labels on a form or report display descriptive text such as titles, captions, or brief instructions.
types.remarks: Labels have certain characteristics: - Labels don't display values from fields or expressions. - Labels are always unbound. - Labels don't change as you move from record to record. A label can be attached to another control. When you create a text box, for example, it has an attached label that displays a caption for that text box. This label appears as a column heading in the Datasheet view of a form. When you create a label by using the Label tool, the label stands on its own-it isn't attached to any other control. You use stand-alone labels for information such as the title of a form or report or for other descriptive text. Stand-alone labels don't appear in Datasheet view.

types.name: ListBox
types.description: This object corresponds to a list box control. The list box control displays a list of values or alternatives.
types.remarks: In many cases, it's quicker and easier to select a value from a list than to remember a value to type. A list of choices also helps ensure that the value that's entered in a field is correct. The list in a list box consists of rows of data. Rows can have one or more columns, which can appear with or without headings, as shown in the following diagram. !Multi-column list box If a multiple-column list box is bound, Microsoft Access stores the values from one of the columns. Use an unbound list box to store a value that you can use with another control. For example, you could use an unbound list box to limit the values in another list box or in a custom dialog box. You could also use an unbound list box to find a record based on the value that you select in the list box. If you don't have room on your form to display a list box, or if you want to be able to type new values as well as select values from a list, use a combo box instead of a list box.
types.example:
Private Sub FilterBy_Change()

    Dim sql As String

    'This will match any entry in the list that begins with what the user
    'has typed in the FilterBy control
    sql = "SELECT ColorID, ColorName FROM Colors WHERE ColorName Like '" & Me.FilterBy.Text & "*' ORDER BY ColorName"

    'If you want to match any part of the string then add wildcard (*) before
    'the FilterBy.Text, too:
    'sql = "SELECT ColorID, ColorName FROM Colors WHERE ColorName Like '*" & Me.FilterBy.Text & "*' ORDER BY ColorName"

    Me.ColorID.RowSource = sql

End Sub

types.name: MacroError
types.description: Represents the properties of a run-time error that occurs in a macro.
types.remarks: When an error occurs in a macro, information about the error is stored in the MacroError object. If you have not used the OnError action to suppress error messages, the macro stops and the error information is displayed in a standard error message. However, if you have used the OnError action to suppress error messages, you may want to use the information stored in the MacroError object in a condition or a custom error message. After an error has been handled, the information in the MacroError object is out of date, so it is a good idea to clear the object by using the ClearMacroError action. This resets the error number in the MacroError object back to zero, and clears any other information about the error that is stored in the object, such as the error description, macro name, action name, condition, and arguments. This way, you can inspect the MacroError object again later to see if another error has occurred. The MacroError object contains information about only one error at a time. If more than one error has occurred in a macro, the MacroError object contains information about only the last one.

properties.name: Condition

properties.name: ActionName
properties.description: Gets the name of the macro action that was executing when an error occurred. Read-only.

properties.name: Arguments
properties.description: Gets the arguments specified for the macro action that was executing when an error occurred. Read-only String.

properties.name: Description
properties.description: Gets the text that represents the current error message. Read-only String.

properties.name: Number
properties.description: Gets the current error number. Read-only Long.

properties.name: MacroName
properties.description: Gets the name of the macro that was running when an error occurred. Read-only String.

types.name: Module
types.description: A Module object refers to a standard module or a class module.
types.remarks: Microsoft Access includes class modules that are not associated with any object, and form modules and report modules, which are associated with a form or report. To determine whether a Module object represents a standard module or a class module from code, check the Module object's Type property. The Modules collection contains all open Module objects, regardless of their type. Modules in the Modules collection can be compiled or uncompiled. To return a reference to a particular standard or class Module object in the Modules collection, use any of the following syntax forms. The following example returns a reference to a standard Module object and assigns it to an object variable. Note that the brackets enclosing the name of the Module object are necessary only if the name of the Module object includes spaces. The next example returns a reference to a form Module object and assigns it to an object variable. To refer to a specific form or report module, you can also use the Form or Report object's Module property. The following example also returns a reference to the Module object associated with an Employees form and assigns it to an object variable.

methods.name: Find
methods.signature: Find(Target As String, StartLine As Long, StartColumn As Long, EndLine As Long, EndColumn As Long, [WholeWord As Boolean], [MatchCase As Boolean], [PatternSearch As Boolean]) As Boolean
methods.description: Finds specified text in a standard module or class module.

parameters.name: Target
parameters.description: The text that you want to find.

parameters.name: StartLine
parameters.description: The line on which to begin searching. If a match is found, the value of the _StartLine_ argument is set to the line on which the beginning character of the matching text is found.

parameters.name: StartColumn
parameters.description: The column on which to begin searching. Each character in a line is in a separate column, beginning with zero on the left side of the module. If a match is found, the value of the _StartColumn_ argument is set to the column in which the beginning character of the matching text is found.

parameters.name: EndLine
parameters.description: The line on which to stop searching. If a match is found, the value of the _EndLine_ argument is set to the line on which the ending character of the matching text is found.

parameters.name: EndColumn
parameters.description: The column on which to stop searching. If a match is found, the value of the _EndColumn_ argument is set to the column in which the beginning character of the matching text is found.

parameters.name: WholeWord
parameters.description: True results in a search for whole words only. The default is False.

parameters.name: MatchCase
parameters.description: True results in a search for words with case matching the _Target_ argument. The default is False.

parameters.name: PatternSearch
parameters.description: True results in a search in which the _Target_ argument may contain wildcard characters such as an asterisk () or a question mark (?). The default is False**.

types.name: Modules
types.description: The Modules collection contains all open standard modules and class modules in a Microsoft Access database.
types.remarks: All open modules are included in the Modules collection, whether they are uncompiled, compiled, or in break mode, or contain the code that's running. To determine whether an individual Module object represents a standard module or a class module, check the Module object's Type property. The Modules collection belongs to the Microsoft Access Application object. Individual Module objects in the Modules collection are indexed beginning with zero.
types.example:
Sub PrintOpenModuleNames()
 Dim i As Integer
 Dim modOpenModules As Modules

 Set modOpenModules = Application.Modules

 For i = 0 To modOpenModules.Count - 1

 Debug.Print modOpenModules(i).Name

 Next
End Sub

parameters.name: KeyCode
parameters.description: A key code, such as vbKeyF1 (the F1 key) or vbKeyHome (the Home key). To specify key codes, use the intrinsic constants shown in the Object Browser. You can prevent an object from receiving a keystroke by setting _KeyCode_ to 0.

This event also occurs if you send an ANSI keystroke to a form or control by using the SendKeys action in a macro or the SendKeys statement in Visual Basic.

parameters.name: KeyCode
parameters.description: A key code, such as vbKeyF1 (the F1 key) or vbKeyHome (the Home key). To specify key codes, use the intrinsic constants shown in the Object Browser. You can prevent an object from receiving a keystroke by setting _KeyCode_ to 0.

types.name: ObjectFrame
types.description: This object corresponds to an unbound object frame. The unbound object frame control displays a picture, chart, or any OLE object not stored in a table.
types.remarks: For example, you can use an unbound object frame to display a chart that you created and stored in Graph. This control allows you to create or edit the object from within a Microsoft Access form or report by using the application in which the object was originally created. To display objects that are stored in an Access database, use a BoundObjectFrame object. The object in an unbound object frame is the same for every record. The unbound object frame can display linked or embedded objects. Use the unbound object frame or an image control to display unbound pictures in a form or report. The advantage of using the unbound object frame is that you can edit the object directly from the form or report. The advantage of using the image control is that it's faster to display.

types.name: OptionGroup
types.description: An option group on a form or report displays a limited set of alternatives. An option group makes selecting a value easy because you can choose the value that you want. Only one option in an option group can be selected at a time.
types.remarks: An option group consists of a group frame and a set of check boxes, toggle buttons, or option buttons. If an option group is bound to a field, only the group frame itself is bound to the field, not the check boxes, toggle buttons, or option buttons inside the frame. Instead of setting the ControlSource property for each control in the option group, you set the OptionValue property of each check box, toggle button, or option button to a number that's meaningful for the field to which the group frame is bound. When you select an option in an option group, Microsoft Access sets the value of the field to which the option group is bound to the value of the selected option's OptionValue property. An option group can also be set to an expression, or it can be unbound. Use an unbound option group in a custom dialog box to accept user input and then carry out an action based on that input.

types.name: Page
types.description: A Page object corresponds to an individual page on a tab control.
types.remarks: A Page object is a member of a tab control's Pages collection. To return a reference to a particular Page object in the Pages collection, use any of the following syntax forms. You can create, move, or delete Page objects and set their properties either in Visual Basic or in form Design view. To create a new Page object in Visual Basic, use the Add method of the Pages collection. To delete a Page object, use the Remove method of the Pages collection. To create a new Page object in form Design view, right-click the tab control and then choose Insert Page on the shortcut menu. You can also copy an existing page and paste it. You can set the properties of the new Page object in form Design view by using the property sheet. Each Page object has a PageIndex property that indicates its position within the Pages collection. The Value property of the tab control is equal to the PageIndex property of the current page. Use these properties to determine which page is currently selected after the user has switched from one page to another, or to change the order in which the pages appear in the control. A Page object is also a type of Control object.

types.name: Pages
types.description: The Pages collection contains all Page objects in a tab control.
types.remarks: The Pages collection is a special kind of Controls collection belonging to the tab control. It contains Page objects, which are controls. The Pages collection differs from a typical Controls collection in that you can add and remove Page objects by using methods of the Pages collection. To add a new Page object to the Pages collection from Visual Basic, use the Add method. To remove an existing Page object, use the Remove method. To count the number of Page objects in the Pages collection, use the Count property. You can also use the CreateControl method to add a Page object to the Pages collection of a tab control. To do this, you must specify the name of the tab control for the _Parent_ argument of the CreateControl function. The ControlType property constant for a Page object is acPage. You can enumerate through the Pages collection by using the For Each...Next statement. Individual Page objects in the Pages collection are indexed beginning with zero.

parameters.name: Item

types.name: Printer
types.description: A Printer object corresponds to a printer available on your system.
types.remarks: A Printer object is a member of the Printers collection. To return a reference to a particular Printer object in the Printers collection, use any of the following syntax forms. Use the properties of the Printer object to set the printing characteristics for any of the printers available on your system. Use the ColorMode, Copies, Duplex, Orientation, PaperBin, PaperSize, and PrintQuality properties to specify print settings for a particular printer. Use the LeftMargin, RightMargin, TopMargin, BottomMargin, ColumnSpacing, RowSpacing, DataOnly, DefaultSize, ItemLayout, ItemsAcross, ItemSizeHeight, and ItemSizeWidth properties to specify how Microsoft Access should format the appearance of data on printed pages. Use the DeviceName, DriverName, and Port properties to return system information about a particular printer.
types.example:
Dim prtFirst As Printer

Set prtFirst = Application.Printers(0)

With prtFirst
 MsgBox "Device name: " & .DeviceName & vbCr _
 & "Driver name: " & .DriverName & vbCr _
 & "Port: " & .Port
End With

types.name: Printers

types.remarks: Use the Printers property of the Application object to return the Printers collection. You can enumerate through the Printers collection by using the For Each...Next statement. Refer to an individual Printer object in the Printers collection either by referring to the printer by name, or by referring to its index within the collection. The Printers collection is indexed beginning with zero. If you refer to a printer by its index, the first printer is Printers(0), the second printer is Printers(1), and so on. You can't add or delete a Printer object from the Printers collection.

 & "Driver name: " & .DriverName & vbCr _
 & "Port: " & .Port
 End With
Next prtLoop

types.name: Properties
types.description: The Properties collection contains all the built-in properties in an instance of an open form, report, or control. These properties uniquely characterize that instance of the object.
types.remarks: Use the Properties collection in Visual Basic or in an expression to refer to form, report, or control properties on forms or reports that are currently open. Use the Properties collection of an object to enumerate the object's built-in properties. You don't need to know beforehand exactly which properties exist or what their characteristics (Name and Value properties) are to manipulate them.
types.example:
Sub AllOpenForms()
 Dim frm As Form, prp As Property

 ' Enumerate Forms collection.
 For Each frm In Forms
 ' Print name of form.
 Debug.Print frm.Name
 ' Enumerate Properties collection of each form.
 For Each prp In frm.Properties
 ' Print name of each property.
 Debug.Print prp.Name; " = "; prp.Value
 Next prp
 Next frm
End Sub

types.name: Reference
types.description: The Reference object refers to a reference set to another application's or project's type library.
types.remarks: When you create a Reference object, you set a reference dynamically from Visual Basic. The Reference object is a member of the References collection. To refer to a particular Reference object in the References collection, use any of the following syntax forms. The following example refers to the Reference object that represents the reference to the Microsoft Access type library.

types.name: References
types.description: The References collection contains Reference objects representing each reference that's currently set.
types.remarks: The Reference objects in the References collection correspond to the list of references in the References dialog box, available by choosing References on the Tools menu. Each Reference object represents one selected reference in the list. References that appear in the References dialog box but haven't been selected aren't in the References collection. You can enumerate through the References collection by using the For Each...Next statement. The References collection belongs to the Microsoft Access Application object. Individual Reference objects in the References collection are indexed beginning with 1.

If a numeric expression, the _var_ argument must be a number from 1 to the value of the collection's Count property. If a string expression, the _var_ argument must be the name of a member of the collection.

types.name: Report
types.description: A Report object refers to a particular Microsoft Access report.
types.remarks: A Report object is a member of the Reports collection, which is a collection of all currently open reports. Within the Reports collection, individual reports are indexed beginning with zero. Refer to an individual Report object in the Reports collection either by referring to the report by name, or by referring to its index within the collection. If the report name includes a space, the name must be surrounded by brackets ([ ]).
types.example:
Private Sub Report_NoData(Cancel As Integer)

    'Add code here that will be executed if no data
